Virender Singh, Judge.

ApplicantSanjeev Kumar @ Sanju has filed the present application, under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (hereinafter referred to as 'BNSS'), for releasing him on bail,
during the pendency of trial, arising out of FIR No.45 of 2024, dated 22.05.2024, registered under Sections 376, 354A and 506 of the Indian Penal Code (hereinafter referred to Whether Reporters of local papers may be allowed to see the judgment?

Yes. 
2 2025:HHC:16779 as the 'IPC') and Sections 4 and 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter referred to as 'POCSO Act'),

with Police Station Rakkar, District Kangra, H.P.
2.
According to the applicant, he is innocent person and has falsely been impleaded by the Police, in this case, as he has nothing to do with the crime, in question.
3. The applicant has termed the case of the prosecution to be based on the wild imagination and hypothesis.
4. As per the applicant, the investigation, in the present case, is complete and he is no longer required by the Police for interrogation as chargesheet has been filed in the competent Court of law.

5. The applicant has also tried his luck by moving the bail application, before the Court of learned Additional Sessions Judge, Fast Track Special Court (POCSO), Kangra at Dharamshala, District Kangra, 3 2025:HHC:16779 however, his application was dismissed, vide order, dated 01st April,
2025.

sentences.text: 7. On the basis of the above facts, a prayer has been made to release the applicant on bail, during the pendency of the trial.

8. When put to notice, the police has filed the status report, disclosing therein, that on 22nd May,
2024, the child victim, who has been arrayed, in this application as respondent No.2, appeared before the Police, along with her paternal aunt (Bua) and moved a complaint, mentioning therein,
that she is resident of the address, as mentioned in the complaint and studying in +2 class.
She has given her age as 15 years 8 months.

8.2. According to the child victim, she was feeling pain in her stomach, as such, she disclosed this fact to 4 2025:HHC:16779 her grandmother, as her mother left her with her grandmother, when she was a small kid.
Thereafter, her grandmother disclosed this fact to her paternal aunt, who took her to place 'X' for getting her checked up.
On 21.05.2024, she appeared before the doctor, who has disclosed her paternal aunt that the child victim is pregnant.
8.3. On inquiry, the child victim disclosed to her that in the month of January, 2024, Sanju (applicant) came to her house, along with her uncle (Chacha) and he has raped her in her house.
Due to his fear, she has not disclosed this fact to anyone.
According to her, she is carrying the foetus of applicant Sanju, who has raped her.
Thereafter, she has prayed that action be taken against applicant Sanju.
8.4. On the basis of the above facts, the police registered the FIR, in question and the criminal machinery swung into motion.
9. During investigation, the child victim was medicolegally examined and the physical evidence, so 5 2025:HHC:16779 collected by the doctors, was taken into possession.
The pregnancy test of the child victim was found to be positive.
Thereafter, her custody was given to her paternal aunt.
Thereafter the applicant was arrested.
He was also medicolegally examined and the physical evidence so collected was also taken into possession.
10. During investigation, on 23.05.2024, statement of paternal aunt of child victim was recorded and spot was visited at the instance of the child victim.
Photography of the spot was done and the statements of the witnesses were recorded.

11. Thereafter, the child victim was produced before the Court of learned Judicial Magistrate First Class Dehra, where her statement under Section 164 Cr.PC, was got recorded and thereafter Sections 354A and 506 IPC were added, in this case.
12.
During investigation, the applicant has identified the place, where, he has allegedly raped the child victim.
Thereafter, the child victim was sent to Shelter Home, Sakoh.

2 13.

sentences.text: On 07.06.2024, medical termination of pregnancy of the child victim was done and on 14.06.2024, further inquiry was conducted from the child victim, who has disclosed in the supplementary statement that her neighbour Ranu Ram has also raped her.
On 15.06.2024, said Ranu Ram was also associated in the investigation and he was also medicolegally examined and sample was also sent for DNA profile.

14. On 14.06.2024, in the supplementary statement, recorded under Section 161 Cr.PC, the child victim has also named her neighbour Ranu Ram, as the person, who has also raped her, whereas, in her earlier statement recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.PC, this fact has not been mentioned.
15. On 09.07.2024, the statement of child victim was recorded under Section 164 Cr.PC, by producing her in the Court of learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Dehra.

Thereafter,
Section 6 of POCSO Act, was also added in this case and accused Ranu Ram was arrested on 10.07.2024.

As per the DNA report, dated 8.8.2024, the child victim was found to be the biological mother of the foetus, whereas, the DNA profile obtained from the blood sample of applicant Sanjeev Kumar is not consistent as biological father of the DNA profile of the aborted foetus.
Similarly, the DNA profile of accused Ranu Ram was also not found to be the source of the aborted foetus.

17. Accused Ranu Ram has been released on bail by learned Special Judge POCSO Court,
Dharamshala, District Kangra.
18.

entities.text:
Special Judge POCSO Court,
Dharamshala, District Kangra
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
It has also been mentioned in the status report that the child victim has again been inquired, but,
except these two persons, she has not disclosed the name of any other person.

Consequently, the blood samples of her father, her brother, her cousin brother were obtained, which were sent to RFSL Junga and report of the same is still inconclusive, as the DNA profile obtained from the blood samples of Rahul Singh, Rohit Kumar, Nitin and Raj Kumar are not consistent as biological father of the aborted foetus.
Lastly, it has been apprehended in the status report that 7 witnesses have been examined and till date the police is unable to ascertain the biological father of the aborted foetus.
20. On the basis of the above facts, a prayer has been made to dismiss the application.

21. Investigation, in the present case, is complete and the prosecution, till date, has examined 17 witnesses, however, in view of the DNA report, which has been relied upon by the Police, in the status report, the applicant cannot be kept in judicial custody for indefinite period, as, his co accused Ranu Ram, against whom, similar allegations have been levelled by the child victim, has already been released on bail by the learned Special Judge POCSO Court, Dharamshala.

sentences.text: The relief cannot be declined to the applicant, for which, he, otherwise, is entitled to, merely, on the ground that he is permanent resident of Punjab.

23. So far as the other apprehensions, which have been expressed by the police, in the status report,
are 9 2025:HHC:16779 concerned, for those apprehensions, reasonable conditions can be imposed,
in case, the applicant is ordered to be released on bail, during the pendency of the trial.
24. Considering all these facts, this Court is of the view that the bail application is liable to be allowed and is accordingly allowed.

Consequently, the applicant is ordered to be released on bail,
during the pendency of the trial, arising out of FIR No.45 of 2024, dated 22.05.2024, registered under Sections 376, 354A and 506 of the IPC and Sections 4 and 6 of the POCSO Act, with Police Station Rakkar, District Kangra, H.P., on his furnishing personal bond, in the sum of Rs.50,000/,
with one surety, in the like amount, to the satisfaction of learned trial Court.
25.

Any of the observations made herein above shall not be taken as an expression of opinion on the merits of the case as these observations are confined only to the disposal of the present bail application.
27. It is made clear that the respondentState is at liberty to move an appropriate application, in case, any of the bail conditions is found to be violated by the bail applicant/petitioner.

28. The Registry is directed to forward a soft copy of the bail order to the Superintendent of Jail,
Lala Lajpat Rai Open Air Correctional Home, Dharamshala, District Kangra, through email, with a direction to enter the date of grant of bail in the eprison software.
